newsitem.title: UK: Sunbeds worse than sun, report says.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeds worse than sun, report says.

text.p: Half an hour in a sunbed can bombard tan-seekers with as much damaging ultraviolet A radiation as a day at the beach, cancer researchers said on Thursday.
Such tanning in a sunbed can not only age the skin, but can cause damage that leads to skin cancer, Britain's Imperial Cancer Research Fund said in a statement accompanying new guidelines on sunbeds.

"We are concerned that people do not understand the risks they are running by getting a tan -- whether from sunbathing or a sunbed," said Dr Veronique Bataille, a consultant dermatologist for the charity.
"Apart from increasing your risks of skin cancer your skin will also age much faster than someone who does not try to tan."
Sunbeds emit mostly ultraviolet A radiation (UVA) which doctors used to think was safer than the UVB normally associated with sunburns and skin cancer.
But they now know it can damage the middle layer of skin, elastin and collagen -- which leads to wrinkles and sagging.
"Many people mistakenly use sunbeds because they think a tan will help protect them from the sun when on holiday," said Dr Julia Newton-Bishop, another ICRF dermatologist.

"Unfortunately, a tan offers very little protection and one from a sunbed is even less effective than one from the sun as UVA doesn't produce the thickening of the outer layer of skin which helps protect us from sunburn."

Skin cancer rates have soared in recent years in countries like Britain, Australia and New Zealand. Dermatologists say when fair-skinned people take holidays in the sun or emigrate to sunny countries and then sunbathe they greatly increase their risk.
Cancer researchers say there is no such thing as a safe tan, whether from the sun or sunbeds.
